_comment: Tutorial scene plan. Narration is spoken text for the voiceover; 'captions' are the on-screen burnt-in lines (kept short). Each scene is recorded as its own clip so a single step can be re-recorded without touching the rest. Verified against the live site 2026-09-11 — see docs/TUTORIAL.md for the written version.

scenes.title: What WikiBento is
scenes.narration: WikiBento is a dashboard you build yourself, out of live Wikimedia data. There is no login and no server to run: you drag cards onto a grid, point each one at a subject, and it fetches the data straight from the Wikimedia APIs. What you are looking at is the starter board — three cards: pageviews for the Main Page, a link count, and a ranking of the largest Wikipedias. All of it is live.
captions: WikiBento: a dashboard you build from live Wikimedia data
No login. No server. Cards on a grid.

scenes.title: Read a board someone shared
scenes.narration: Boards travel as URLs. This one is the WikiPortraits demo, and the entire configuration is in the link: config equals, followed by a wiki page address. WikiBento fetches that page and builds the board from it. Every card has the same top bar: the i explains where its data comes from, the gear configures it, the arrow refreshes it, and the cross removes it. The name chip next to the title is the card's identity — other cards can refer to it by that name.
captions: A board is a URL: ?config=<wiki page address>
ⓘ where the data comes from · ⚙ settings · ↻ refresh · ✕ remove

scenes.title: Clear it and start your own
scenes.narration: To start your own board, you can clear this one: click Reset, and the board goes back to the same three starter cards. Anything you had is gone, so export first if you want to keep it. From here, everything you add is yours.
captions: ↺ Reset restores the three-card starter board
Export first if you want to keep a board

scenes.title: Add a card and point it at a subject
scenes.narration: Click Add Widget. The picker lists every card type, grouped by category, and you can search it. I will search for pageviews and add Article Pageviews. A new card appears with a placeholder subject. Open its gear to configure it: here is the article field — type or paste the exact article title — and the project selector beside it. Watch the total and the daily bars fill in with real data for that article. Anything you change takes effect immediately.
captions: + Add Widget: search or browse by category
⚙ Configure: set the article, pick the project — it updates live

scenes.title: Move and resize
scenes.url: drag the top bar to move · the corner to resize
scenes.narration: Drag a card by its top bar to move it, and the rest of the board reflows around it. Drag the bottom corner to resize. The grid keeps everything aligned, and each card has a minimum size so it cannot be squashed into something unreadable.
captions: Drag by the top bar to move · drag the corner to resize
The grid keeps the board aligned

scenes.title: Export the board
scenes.narration: When the board looks right, click Export. WikiBento writes the whole thing — every card, its settings, and its position — as a small JSON file. That file is the board: there is nothing else to save.
captions: ⬇ Export writes the whole board as JSON
Cards + settings + positions — that file is the board

scenes.title: Put the JSON where it can be fetched
scenes.narration: That JSON needs a home your browser can read. The easy place is a wiki page: paste it onto a subpage of your user page, and it lives there with the wiki's own history and permissions. WikiBento reads wiki pages through the CORS-enabled MediaWiki API, which is why this works without any extra hosting. This is the page behind the demo board. If you host the file somewhere else instead, it has to allow cross-origin requests — otherwise you will see "could not load dashboard from URL" and the board falls back to the starter set.
captions: Paste the JSON into a wiki page (e.g. your user subpage)
Wiki pages work: the app reads them via the CORS-enabled MediaWiki API
Other hosts must allow cross-origin requests, or the load fails

scenes.title: Load it anywhere
scenes.narration: And that is the payoff. Your wiki page plus config equals is a complete, portable board. Open that URL on any machine, or on a lobby kiosk, and the same dashboard appears. The link is the whole thing: share it, bookmark it, or turn it into a QR code.
captions: The link IS the board — portable, bookmarkable, kiosk-ready
Share it, or make a QR code
